title: This week in recruiting tools: Juicebox buys Fetcher, LinkedIn Hiring Assistant inside iCIMS, Workday ships Candidate Profile and agents
summary: A consolidation week across the recruiting stack: Juicebox agreed to acquire Fetcher's assets, iCIMS wired in LinkedIn's Hiring Assistant, Metaview went deeper into Workday, Workday launched Candidate Profile plus HR agents, Eightfold appointed a new CEO, and Noon published public docs for driving it from AI assistants.

items.headline: Juicebox announced an agreement to acquire Fetcher's assets
items.detail: Announced 6 Oct 2026 (Business Wire; Axios). Fetcher sold batch sourcing on per-role tiers; Juicebox is a natural-language search tool. Fetcher customers should plan for a migration; see Juicebox and Fetcher in the directory and our sourcing-database switching guide.
items.matters: The independent sourcing category keeps shrinking; AI-search vendors are buying customer bases.

items.headline: iCIMS integrated LinkedIn Hiring Assistant into its ATS
items.detail: Announced 14 Oct 2026 (HRTech Series), two weeks after LinkedIn's 'Hiring Assistant 2' update (TLNT, 2 Oct), which focused on smarter matching.
items.matters: LinkedIn's agent now lives inside a major enterprise ATS, so iCIMS customers get an agent without adding a vendor; the seat and InMail credit model is unchanged. Compare in iCIMS and LinkedIn Recruiter.

items.headline: Metaview expanded its Workday integration for Fortune 500 recruiting teams
items.detail: Announced 14 Oct 2026 (Business Wire). Metaview records and structures interviews and is extending that into agentic workflows on Workday data (Metaview review).
items.matters: The ATS is becoming the control plane for recruiting agents; point tools without native Workday or SAP integrations will feel it in enterprise deals.

items.headline: Workday launched Candidate Profile and a set of HR, finance and IT agents
items.detail: Announced 13 Oct 2026 (Workday blog; Investing.com). Candidate Profile is a reusable applicant profile meant to end repeated form-filling.
items.matters: Portable profiles change the apply experience for the largest employers, and Workday's own agent layer now competes directly for third-party automation budget.

items.headline: Eightfold AI named Joe Korngiebel as CEO
items.detail: Announced 13 Oct 2026 (GlobeNewswire). Eightfold sells talent intelligence, matching and rediscovery to large enterprises.
items.matters: CEO changes at platform vendors usually precede packaging and pricing changes; buyers mid-evaluation should ask about the roadmap and contract flexibility.

items.headline: Noon published public MCP docs, a weekly changelog and switch-from guides
items.detail: Published 14 Oct 2026 (noon.ai/changelog). The docs let Claude and ChatGPT users drive Noon's sourcing and outreach tools from their assistant.
items.matters: First vendor in our directory with public AI-assistant (MCP) documentation; expect 'can my assistant run it?' to become a standard RFP line.

directory: New on RecruitmentTools.org this week: vendor-neutral switching guides for teams leaving LinkedIn Recruiter, SeekOut or hireEZ and Gem.

title: This week in recruiting tools: Workday moves to split up Mobley, HireVue adds fraud signals, Remote builds its own screener
summary: A week where the legal and build questions caught up with the stack: Workday asked the court to decertify the Mobley age collective, HireVue shipped fraud detection across interviews and assessments, Remote's people team showed what an in house ATS looks like, Survale plugged candidate feedback into SmartRecruiters on the SAP Store, Dayforce closed on Ribbon, and the staffing numbers from Bullhorn and Recruit Holdings kept climbing.

items.headline: Workday asked the court to decertify the age discrimination collective in Mobley v. Workday
items.detail: Filed 10 Nov 2026 in federal court in San Francisco, as reported by Startup Fortune citing MLex and Forbes. The collective now covers more than 15,000 opt in plaintiffs. A second filing asks Judge Rita Lin to stop the much wider applicant group from pursuing race, sex, age and disability claims together. Workday argues that employers, not Workday, make the hiring decisions and that each customer configures screening differently. This is a motion, not a ruling.
items.matters: Whatever Judge Lin decides will set how much shared liability a screening vendor carries for its customers' outcomes. Buyers should keep asking vendors for configuration logs and adverse impact reporting now rather than after a ruling.

items.headline: HireVue launched advanced fraud detection inside its platform
items.detail: Announced 10 Nov 2026 via PR Newswire (release text). The new capabilities connect identity, location and behavioral signals across interviews and assessments and present the evidence to hiring teams rather than issuing a verdict on their own.
items.matters: Candidate fraud checks are moving from separate point tools into the interview and assessment layer. Teams already paying for HireVue should test this before buying a standalone identity product.

items.headline: Remote's HR team replaced outside vendors with tools it built using AI, starting with a CV screener
items.detail: Reported 10 Nov 2026 by HR Brew. The project began as a January off site dare between founder Job van der Voort and CPO Barbara Matthews to build an ATS in house; a resume screener came first and grew into a wider rebuild of the internal stack, one homegrown tool at a time.
items.matters: Most companies will not build an ATS, but a credible build option changes renewal conversations. Expect more buyers to ask why a screening add on costs what it does.

items.headline: Survale joined SAP PartnerEdge and listed its SmartRecruiters integration on the SAP Store
items.detail: Announced 10 Nov 2026 (citybuzz). Status changes in SmartRecruiters trigger pulse surveys at each hiring stage, and responses are tied to job, location, source and hiring manager data.
items.matters: SmartRecruiters customers inside the SAP estate get a procurement path for candidate feedback that does not need a separate contract negotiation.

items.headline: Dayforce closed its acquisition of the AI interviewing platform Ribbon
items.detail: Reported 5 Nov 2026 by HR Brew. Ribbon founder Arsham Ghahramani builds conversational AI voice interviews; Dayforce adds them to its HCM suite.
items.matters: Another suite has bought its AI interviewer instead of partnering, which narrows the field of standalone voice screening vendors that integrate everywhere.

items.headline: US staffing hours rose 12% year over year in the week ended 31 October
items.detail: From the SIA | Bullhorn Staffing Indicator published 10 Nov 2026: commercial hours up 13%, professional up 10% and industrial up 18% on the prior year, another year to date high.
items.matters: Agencies heading into peak season on rising hours tend to add recruiters and seats, so renewal leverage sits with vendors through year end.

items.headline: Recruit Holdings reported record quarterly revenue with its HR Technology unit leading
items.detail: Results for the quarter ended 30 Sep 2026, reported 11 Nov by Staffing Industry Analysts: revenue of JPY 1.09 trillion, about USD 6.88 billion, up 19.7%. Recruit is the parent of Indeed.
items.matters: Indeed's owner is growing fast enough to keep pushing sponsored job pricing and its own screening features, which affects every ATS that posts there.
